stimulus.source_note: Theodor de Bry, engraving of Indigenous workers in the Potosi silver mine, 1590, public domain; the image is a European engraving made by an artist who never visited the Americas.
stimulus.text: The engraving shows Indigenous workers inside the silver mine at Potosi, in the Andes mountains of South America. Workers climb ladders carrying baskets of ore on their backs, while others break rock with tools below. Spanish overseers stand among them. The mine opened in 1545 and became the richest source of silver in the Spanish Empire.

stem: After 1545, the silver mines at Potosi produced enormous wealth that flowed into Spanish treasuries and across the world economy. Which broader development best explains the historical significance of Potosi's silver?

options.text: It drew thousands of European migrants to settle the high Andes.
It financed Spain's military and state power, and forced rival crowns to spend in response.
It allowed Spain to abolish the encomienda labor system at once.
It ended European dependence on Asian trade goods and markets.

instruction: Pick one option from the stimulus and stem only. Do not open the question file.
